chapter_title: Measurement and Interpretation of Stress-Strain and Stiffness Properties

sections.title: Uses and Measurement of Small-Strain Stiffness
sections.summary: Stiffness properties are used for settlement of shallow foundations on sands (Schmertmann 1970), deflection analysis, dynamic analysis (site amplification, liquefaction), pavement design (subgrade modulus), and p-y analysis of laterally loaded piles. Small-strain shear modulus Gmax is the upper bound; Gmax = ρVs² where Vs = shear wave velocity. Gmax from in situ seismic tests: crosshole (ASTM D4428), downhole, seismic CPT (SCPT), suspension logging, and surface wave methods (MASW, passive arrays). MASW resolves Vs profiles to ~30 m depth. Vs30 (average Vs in upper 30 m) is the AASHTO/IBC site classification parameter.
sections.body:
Uses for stiffness properties: (1) settlement analysis for shallow foundations on sands and granular soils; (2) deflection analysis of structures; (3) dynamic analysis — site response, liquefaction assessment, and site amplification (Vs30 for site classification); (4) pavement subgrade modulus; (5) p-y analysis for laterally loaded piles; (6) evaluation of ground vibrations.

Small-strain stiffness (Gmax): Maximum shear stiffness at very small strains (<0.001%). Gmax = ρ × Vs² where Vs = shear wave velocity and ρ = mass density. Shear wave velocity Vs is the most direct measurement of Gmax. Also expressed as Emax = 2(1+ν) × Gmax where ν = Poisson's ratio (~0.2–0.35 for most soils).

In situ seismic methods: (1) Crosshole test (ASTM D4428): Source and receivers in separate boreholes at same depth; measures Vs and Vp at specific depths; most accurate but requires ≥2 boreholes. (2) Downhole test: Single borehole receiver, surface source; multiple depths. (3) Seismic CPT (SCPT): Seismic source at surface, geophone in CPT module; provides Vs profile with each push. (4) Suspension logging: Borehole probe with source and receivers; good for deep profiles. (5) Surface wave methods: MASW (Multichannel Analysis of Surface Waves) — active source at surface; resolves Vs profile to ~30 m; no boreholes required. Passive methods (ReMi, SPAC) extend to greater depths. Vs30 = average Vs in upper 30 m per AASHTO/IBC site class.
key_points: Gmax = ρVs²; Vs from seismic testing is the most reliable measurement of Gmax
Vs30 (average Vs in upper 30 m) is AASHTO/IBC site classification parameter for seismic site class
MASW: surface wave method; no boreholes needed; depth to ~30 m; passive methods extend deeper
Crosshole test (ASTM D4428): most accurate in situ Vs measurement; requires ≥2 boreholes

sections.title: Gmax Correlations and Modulus Degradation
sections.summary: Gmax from laboratory and indirect methods: resonant column (RC) and torsional shear (TS) tests measure small-strain Gmax and modulus reduction curves. Hardin-Richart (1963): Gmax = A × F(e) × σ'm^n (Eq 8.7) for coarse-grained soils. Gmax from SPT N60: Imai and Tonouchi (1982) Gmax = 325 × N60^0.68 (kPa, sand); Table 8-6. Gmax from CPT/CPTU: various correlations in Table 8-7/8-8. Modulus reduction at working strains: G/Gmax vs. shear strain curve; Es for shallow foundation settlement from G/Gmax. Pressuremeter: Ep = 2(1+ν) × Vo × (ΔP/ΔV). Constrained modulus M from CPT: M = α × qc (Table 10-11 for α).
sections.body:
Laboratory measurement of Gmax: Resonant column (RC) test and torsional shear (TS) test measure Gmax at very small strains and modulus reduction curves at larger strains up to about 0.1%. Both require high quality undisturbed specimens.

Gmax correlation with stress and void ratio (Hardin and Richart 1963, Eq 8.7): Gmax = A × F(e) × σ'm^n where A = soil stiffness constant, F(e) = void ratio function, σ'm = mean effective stress, n = stress exponent. Table 8-2 provides A, F(e), and n for coarse-grained soils.

Gmax from SPT N60 (indirect, Table 8-6): Examples — Imai and Tonouchi (1982): Gmax = 325 × N60^0.68 (kPa, sand). Multiple alternative correlations available; all carry substantial uncertainty.

Gmax from CPT (indirect, Tables 8-7, 8-8): Various correlations relating Gmax and Vs to measured qt, fs, and σ'vo. From DMT: Gmax estimated from ED (dilatometer modulus) ratio, approximate only.

Modulus reduction: G/Gmax decreases from 1.0 at very small strains to near 0 at large strains. Working strains for most structures are typically 0.01–0.3%. Figure 8-15 shows recommended modulus degradation ratios. Design modulus Es = G/Gmax × 2(1+ν)/(1+ν/other) at appropriate strain level. Pressuremeter: Ep = 2(1+ν) × Vo × (ΔP/ΔV) over appropriate stress increment. DMT constrained modulus: MDMT = RM × ED where RM is a function of ID and KD (Marchetti 2001). p-y models: Table 8-13 lists common p-y models for lateral pile analysis.
key_points: Hardin-Richart (1963): Gmax = A × F(e) × σ'm^n; Table 8-2 for coarse-grained soils
Gmax from SPT: substantial uncertainty; Imai and Tonouchi (1982) Gmax = 325N60^0.68 (kPa, sand)
Modulus degradation curve G/Gmax vs. strain; working strains for structures typically 0.01–0.3%
Constrained modulus from CPT: M = α × qc; α from Table 10-11
